developers.scale_note: Founded 2000; ~3 msf of completed projects with ~6 msf reported in the pipeline. developers.delivery_reputation: Better known for commercial/IT park development than for residential volume. Residential delivery evidence is thin and mixed: company materials claim strict quality control and timely completion, while a documented buyer account reports an OMR project with possession due January 2017 still undelivered as of December 2017, alongside unresponsive engineering and customer service. No regulatory action found; the small residential sample size means neither a clean nor a poor record can be asserted with confidence.

developers.scale_note: Founded 1995 by T. Chitty Babu; company claims 171 delivered projects and 6,000+ customers across Tamil Nadu. Operating revenue band of Rs 100-500 crore for FY ending March 2023 per Tofler.
developers.delivery_reputation: Long-standing Chennai developer known for design-led projects including the landmark Akshaya Abov tower. This research did not surface any TNRERA adjudication, NCLT proceeding or documented systemic delay pattern against Akshaya Private Limited — an NCLT Chennai matter found in searches related to a similarly named but unrelated entity. developers.name: Alliance Group
developers.scale_note: Parent of the Urbanrise brand, founded 2004 by Manoj Namburu; 42 msf worth ~Rs 24,000 crore under execution and 22,000+ homes delivered — Chennai is its single largest market, where the Alliance name carries its premium/mid portfolio (Orchid Springs, Bay Woods, Galleria Residences, Humming Gardens) while Urbanrise carries volume housing.
developers.delivery_reputation: Same promoter and execution platform as Urbanrise — Chennai listings use both names interchangeably, so buyers filtering by developer should treat 'Alliance' and 'Urbanrise' as one counterparty. Its older Chennai premium projects (OMR, Padur, Kelambakkam belt) are broadly regarded as delivered, but consumer-forum complaint threads under the Alliance Group name run back several years on refunds and possession timing. No Tamil Nadu regulatory action against the Alliance entity was found; the adjudicated order on record is against the Urbanrise entity in Telangana.
red_flags: Long-running consumer-forum complaint thread against Alliance Infrastructure Projects / Alliance Group on refunds and possession delays (consumercomplaints.in; unadjudicated)
developers.financial_note: Private; no audited FY26 figures found.
developers.recent_activity_2025_2026: Group activity in 2025-26 is channelled largely through the Urbanrise brand across Chennai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru; no separate Alliance-branded Chennai capital event found.

developers.name: Appaswamy Real Estates
developers.scale_note: Chennai's oldest surviving branded apartment developer — founded 1959, credited with introducing apartment living to Chennai in the 1960s; 53 residential and commercial projects, 46 of them in Chennai, plus a hospitality arm (The Residency group, St Regis Maldives).
developers.delivery_reputation: One of the strongest reputations in the Chennai market for build quality and title cleanliness, especially in the central/inner-city premium segment (Mylapore, Nungambakkam, Guindy, Koyambedu). Marketed positioning claims timely delivery, and completion certificates are on record for recent projects (Coimbatore villa project CC 04.02.2025; Guindy apartment CC 23.06.2026). Independent third-party audits of delay performance are scarce, so the reputation rests largely on longevity and buyer word-of-mouth rather than published data.
developers.recent_activity_2025_2026: New Chennai launches include a Luz Church Road (Mylapore) 3 and 4 BHK project RERA-registered 08.08.2025, a Nungambakkam 3 BHK project, and a Koyambedu 3 and 4 BHK project RERA-registered 03.07.2026; Guindy project received completion certificate 23.06.2026.

developers.scale_note: BSE-listed (scrip 531381) Chennai developer with 10+ msf delivered across 40+ residential and commercial projects; 43+ completed and 3 ongoing residential projects tracked in Chennai. Ongoing project GDV reported above Rs 11,250 crore.
developers.delivery_reputation: Established listed Chennai player whose credibility is reinforced by being chosen as the local JV partner by both Prestige Estates (Padi) and, historically, Unitech (North Town). developers.financial_note: FY26 pre-sales Rs 513.7 crore, up 28% YoY; Q4 FY26 pre-sales Rs 183.3 crore, up 46% QoQ and 15% YoY; ongoing project GDV above Rs 11,250 crore. developers.name: Casagrand
developers.scale_note: As of 30 June 2025 the company reported 103 completed projects (21.79 msf), 57 ongoing (44.10 msf) and 21 forthcoming (23.81 msf) — roughly 90 msf of total saleable area across Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Coimbatore and Pune.
developers.delivery_reputation: By volume Casagrand is Chennai's largest residential developer — IPO materials cite ~25% share of Chennai project launches and ~18% of demand between 2017 and mid-2025 — and it has delivered 100+ projects. Against that, buyer forums and legal-advice sites carry a consistent pattern of complaints about repeated TNRERA completion-date extensions (COVID/flood grounds), refusal to pay contractual delay compensation once an extension is granted, registration withheld until ~95% payment, and refusal to permit third-party handover audits. Construction-quality gripes (wall finish, car-park allocation discrepancies) appear but are not regulator-adjudicated.
red_flags: TNRERA cancelled the registration of Casagrand's 'Bloom' project at Thirumudivakkam and fined the company Rs 30 lakh for misrepresentation — registering a villa township as a mere plotted layout (reported Feb 2020, per Constro Facilitator)
Widely reported buyer complaints of multi-year RERA deadline extensions with delay compensation declined (forum/consumer-site reports, not adjudicated)
developers.financial_note: Revenue above Rs 1,000 crore for FY ending March 2025; per Tracxn, revenue grew ~4% while PAT fell ~9% between FY24 and FY25. Refiled DRHP with SEBI on 29 Dec 2025; SEBI approval received 8 June 2026 for a Rs 1,220 crore book-built IPO (Rs 1,200 cr fresh issue + Rs 20 cr OFS), proceeds largely earmarked for repaying/prepaying borrowings.
developers.recent_activity_2025_2026: Launched Casagrand Ventra, a premium high-rise community in West Chennai; opened a Mumbai development office in early 2026; SEBI cleared its IPO in June 2026 after a third filing attempt.

developers.name: Ceebros
developers.scale_note: Founded 1980; 88+ residential projects tracked in Chennai plus hospitality and commercial assets — a premium, moderate-volume developer rather than a mass-market one.
developers.delivery_reputation: One of the better-regarded delivery names in Chennai's premium segment, repeatedly grouped with Appaswamy and KG in market commentary as builders whose projects command better resale value, easier bank financing and reliable completion. Notably it has sold to three successive generations of the same families, which is a meaningful trust signal in this market. Some isolated negative reviews exist on MouthShut but they read as customer-service grievances rather than delivery failures. No regulatory action found.
developers.recent_activity_2025_2026: Continues premium Chennai development with ongoing projects listed on portals; no major capital event or landmark launch surfaced for 2025-2026.

developers.scale_note: 42+ years in the market with ~46 lakh sqft (~4.6 msf) built and homes delivered to 3,800+ families across 30 residential and commercial projects, all in Chennai.
developers.delivery_reputation: A gap exists between the company's own testimonials — which emphasise timely delivery and quality — and independent buyer accounts. developers.name: Jain Housing
developers.scale_note: High-volume legacy Chennai builder with a large delivered portfolio concentrated in the OMR, Pallavaram and southern suburbs belt (Pebble Brook, Green Acres, Nakshatra, Aadhya).
developers.delivery_reputation: One of the most complaint-heavy names in Chennai residential. developers.name: Olympia Group
developers.scale_note: Mixed residential-plus-commercial Chennai developer; 2,000+ homes delivered and a portfolio of IGBC/LEED-certified assets including Olympia Technology Park, once certified as the largest LEED Gold rated green building in the world.
developers.delivery_reputation: Delivery record on its flagship OMR residential township is documented as poor in the early cycle: the Amber block at Olympia Opaline, Navalur, was promised for April 2011 and delivered in April 2013, and buyer forums record complaints across multiple blocks about delays, construction quality and withheld amenities, with balance-payment demands issued before fit-out handover and delay compensation contested. developers.delivery_reputation: This is the clearest distressed case in the Chennai set. Possession at Metrozone was originally due in 2014 with contractual delay interest, and reporting records that the company neither handed over nor paid interest despite follow-up. The project is now reported complete and ready to move, but the corporate entities behind it are in insolvency and under criminal investigation, so title, association handover, common-area completion and any pending buyer dues warrant specialist legal review before transacting.
red_flags: NCLT Chennai admitted an insolvency petition by IDBI Trusteeship Services against Ozone Homes Pvt Ltd on 10 October 2025, commencing CIRP over a Rs 389.20 crore default on secured redeemable non-convertible debentures (LiveLaw, BW Legal World)

CBI FIR alleging criminal conspiracy between the developer and financial institutions over Metrozone subvention-scheme home loans — banks reportedly disbursed full loans in buyers' names directly to the developer without proper sale agreements, in violation of RBI and NHB norms, leaving buyers pursued for EMIs (per reporting on the CBI probe)

Enforcement Directorate searched Ozone Urbana Infra Developers in a probe into an alleged Rs 4,000 crore real-estate scam (Moneylife); homebuyer groups have publicly alleged the same and called for government intervention
NCLT Chennai has adjudicated Section 7 IBC and Companies Act matters involving Ozone Projects Pvt Ltd brought by homebuyers/allottees
developers.financial_note: Rs 389.20 crore NCD default triggering CIRP against Ozone Homes Pvt Ltd; no reliable current group financials available.
developers.recent_activity_2025_2026: CIRP commenced against Ozone Homes Pvt Ltd in October 2025; Metrozone Anna Nagar reported completed and ready-to-move as of May 2026, with the CBI investigation into the subvention-loan arrangements ongoing.

developers.name: Unitech
developers.scale_note: Once among India's largest developers, now run by a government-appointed board under Supreme Court supervision. Chennai exposure is limited to the ~49-acre 'North Town' project developed in partnership with Arihant, comprising roughly 2,400 flats and villas.
developers.delivery_reputation: The most comprehensively documented governance failure in Indian real estate: the board was superseded and taken over by government appointees in 2020 following findings of widespread financial wrongdoing, with promoters facing criminal proceedings. Completion of legacy projects now runs through a Supreme Court-approved revised payment plan (order dated 03.11.2023) under which the government-appointed management repeatedly asks buyers to pay balance dues in instalments. Any Chennai North Town exposure is a legacy workout, not a live development relationship.
red_flags: Board superseded and taken over by government appointees under Supreme Court order in January 2020 following findings of widespread financial wrongdoing
Legacy project completion proceeds only under a Supreme Court-approved Revised Payment Plan dated 03.11.2023, administered by government-appointed management
Chennai North Town required external rescue funding — Unitech raised ~Rs 70 crore from a Piramal group real estate fund in 2015 to complete construction (PTI/Business Standard)
developers.financial_note: Under government-appointed management; no normal financial reporting. Funding for legacy completion comes from buyer instalments under the SC-approved plan.
developers.recent_activity_2025_2026: Supreme Court has continued to unblock construction on Noida/Greater Noida projects by directing planning authorities to sanction revised building plans; no fresh Chennai activity found — Chennai exposure is confined to completing the legacy North Town partnership with Arihant.
